keyword: what happens if you file taxes late
claims: Filing taxes late usually results in a failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid taxes per month up to 25%
Filing taxes late usually results in a failure-to-pay penalty of 0.5% per month
If you are owed a refund, there is no penalty
If you are owed a refund, you have three years from the deadline to file and claim it
The penalty for not filing is 5% per month
The penalty for not paying is 0.5% per month
If both penalties apply, the combined penalty is 5% each month
The IRS charges interest on underpayments at the federal short-term rate plus 3%
The IRS may file a substitute return on your behalf
A substitute return often misses out on deductions and credits you are entitled to
The penalty stops accruing once you file
You can file Form 4868 for an automatic extension until October 15
Form 4868 does not extend the time to pay taxes owed
The IRS offers installment agreements to pay off your balance over time
